passage.title: A Space for the River
passage.text:
For many years, the people of Bellford regarded their river mainly as a threat. High walls separated it from nearby streets, and a narrow channel carried water quickly through the center of town. The design had protected buildings during many ordinary storms. However, as the town expanded, more roofs and paved surfaces prevented rain from soaking into the ground. Water reached the river faster, and maintaining safety became increasingly difficult.

One response would have been to make the walls higher. Instead, planners proposed allowing the river more room at a former industrial site upstream. Old warehouses there had been removed, leaving land that could temporarily hold water during heavy rain. In dry weather, most of the area could be used as a public park. The proposal did not eliminate the need for walls elsewhere; it was intended to complement existing defenses.

Some residents objected that a park designed to flood was a waste of money. They feared that equipment would be damaged and the area would be closed too often. The design team responded by placing expensive electrical equipment above expected water levels and choosing surfaces that could be cleaned after flooding. Path signs explained that lower routes might close, while a higher route would remain available under most conditions.

A more difficult question concerned who would benefit. The park was near a neighborhood with few green spaces, but many people living there had not attended the early planning meetings. The meetings had been held during working hours and relied on technical presentations. The town changed the schedule and used a temporary model that residents could walk around. This led to requests for better lighting, places to sit, and a safer crossing to the park.

After the park opened, a severe storm tested the design. Water spread across the lower ground as intended, and some paths were closed for cleaning afterward. Officials resisted describing this as a failure of the park: temporary flooding was part of its protective function. At the same time, they acknowledged that the cleanup had taken longer than expected and revised the maintenance plan.

Bellford's experience illustrates why adapting to floods involves more than building a single structure. The physical design, the ability to maintain it, and the ways people understand and use it all matter. A project can serve several purposes, but those purposes need to be explained honestly. passage.title: A Space for the River
passage.text:
For many years, the people of Bellford regarded their river mainly as a threat. High walls separated it from nearby streets, and a narrow channel carried water quickly through the center of town. The design had protected buildings during many ordinary storms. However, as the town expanded, more roofs and paved surfaces prevented rain from soaking into the ground. Water reached the river faster, and maintaining safety became increasingly difficult.

One response would have been to make the walls higher. Instead, planners proposed allowing the river more room at a former industrial site upstream. Old warehouses there had been removed, leaving land that could temporarily hold water during heavy rain. In dry weather, most of the area could be used as a public park. The proposal did not eliminate the need for walls elsewhere; it was intended to complement existing defenses.

Some residents objected that a park designed to flood was a waste of money. They feared that equipment would be damaged and the area would be closed too often. The design team responded by placing expensive electrical equipment above expected water levels and choosing surfaces that could be cleaned after flooding. Path signs explained that lower routes might close, while a higher route would remain available under most conditions.

A more difficult question concerned who would benefit. The park was near a neighborhood with few green spaces, but many people living there had not attended the early planning meetings. The meetings had been held during working hours and relied on technical presentations. The town changed the schedule and used a temporary model that residents could walk around. This led to requests for better lighting, places to sit, and a safer crossing to the park.

After the park opened, a severe storm tested the design. Water spread across the lower ground as intended, and some paths were closed for cleaning afterward. Officials resisted describing this as a failure of the park: temporary flooding was part of its protective function. At the same time, they acknowledged that the cleanup had taken longer than expected and revised the maintenance plan.

Bellford's experience illustrates why adapting to floods involves more than building a single structure. The physical design, the ability to maintain it, and the ways people understand and use it all matter. A project can serve several purposes, but those purposes need to be explained honestly. Calling a floodable park permanently dry would create false expectations; treating it only as empty storage would overlook its everyday value to residents.

items.prompt: 以下の英文を読んで、その内容を英語で要約し、解答欄に記入しなさい。本文にない自分の意見は加えないこと。（目安語数：45〜55語）

passage.title: Rethinking Nighttime Park Lighting
passage.text:
Many cities keep public parks brightly lit throughout the night. Strong white lights help pedestrians see walking paths clearly, give evening commuters a greater sense of security, and deter criminal behavior.

In recent years, however, researchers have pointed out the drawbacks of excessive nighttime lighting. Leaving powerful lamps on until morning consumes large amounts of electricity. In addition, artificial glare disrupts nocturnal insects and confuses migrating birds that rely on natural darkness.

To address these concerns without sacrificing public safety, several municipalities have redesigned their lighting systems. They now install shields that direct light downward onto paths and use motion sensors to dim lamps when nobody is nearby, protecting local ecosystems while saving energy.
passage.translation:
多くの都市では公共の公園を一晩中明るく照らしている。強い白色光は歩行者が歩道をはっきりと見られるようにし、夜間の通行人に安心感を与え、犯罪行為を抑止する。
しかし近年、研究者たちは過度な夜間照明の欠点を指摘している。強力な街灯を朝まで点灯し続けることは大量の電力を消費する。さらに人工的なまぶしさは夜行性の昆虫に悪影響を与え、自然の暗闇に頼る渡り鳥を混乱させる。
公共の安全を損なわずにこれらの懸念へ対処するため、複数の自治体が照明設備を再設計している。光を歩道へ下向きに絞るカバーを取り付け、近くに人がいないときは人感センサーで減光することで、電力を節約しつつ地域の生態系を守っている。

items.model: Bright park lighting at night helps pedestrians walk safely and prevents crime. However, excessive illumination consumes substantial electricity and harms nocturnal insects and migrating birds. Consequently, several cities now use downward-facing shields and motion sensors to conserve energy and protect wildlife while maintaining public safety.
items.translation: 夜間の明るい公園照明は歩行者の安全な通行を助け犯罪を防ぐ。しかし過度な照明は大量の電力を消費し、夜行性の昆虫や渡り鳥に害を与える。そのため複数の都市では現在、下向きカバーと人感センサーを用い、公共の安全を保ちながら節電と野生生物の保護を図っている。
items.explanation: 第1段落の利点（歩行者の安全・防犯）、第2段落の課題（電力消費と昆虫・渡り鳥への悪影響）、第3段落の解決策（下向き遮光カバーと人感センサーによる安全・節電・生態系保護の両立）を45語で端的にまとめています。
rubric: 夜間照明の利点（歩行者の安全・防犯）を簡潔に示した
過度な照明の欠点（電力消費・野生生物への悪影響）を含めた
自治体の改善策（下向き照明・人感センサー）と効果を結んだ
原文の表現を適切に言い換え45〜55語の目安に収めた

items.prompt:
次のTOPICについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ書きなさい。POINTSは理由を書く際の参考として自由に用いてかまいません。（目安語数：80〜100語）
TOPIC: Some people say that companies should encourage employees to take longer summer vacations. What do you think about that?
POINTS:
• Health
• Productivity
• Teamwork
items.model:
I agree that companies should encourage employees to take longer summer vacations.
First, extended rest protects workers' physical and mental health. Working continuously under heavy pressure often leads to exhaustion, whereas spending a full week away from office duties allows employees to recover completely.
Second, longer vacations can improve workplace productivity and teamwork. When employees return refreshed, they concentrate better and generate creative ideas. Moreover, sharing duties while colleagues are away helps teams organize tasks more systematically.
Therefore, promoting longer summer holidays benefits both employees and companies.
items.translation:
私は企業が従業員により長い夏季休暇を取るよう促すべきだという意見に賛成です。
第一に、まとまった休養は働く人の心身の健康を守ります。強い重圧の下で働き続けると疲労につながりやすいですが、職場の業務から丸1週間離れることで完全に回復できます。
第二に、長期休暇は職場の生産性とチームワークを高められます。リフレッシュして復帰すれば集中力が増し創造的な発想が生まれます。さらに同僚の不在中に業務を分担することで、チームはより体系的に仕事を整理できるようになります。
したがって、長い夏休みの推進は従業員と企業の双方に利益をもたらします。
items.explanation: 序論（賛成表明）→本論1（Health：継続勤務による疲労の防止と心身の回復）→本論2（Productivity / Teamwork：復帰後の集中力・創造性向上と業務分担の整理）→結論の4段落構成で87語にまとめています。
rubric: 序論・本論（理由2つ）・結論の明確な段落構成で書いた
2つの理由が互いに重複せず具体的に展開されている
適切な接続表現（First, whereas, Moreover, Therefore等）を用いた
80〜100語の目安に収まっている

items.prompt: The two eyewitnesses gave (     ) accounts of the accident, so police had to check nearby security cameras.

gratefulは「感謝している」。
obedientは「従順な」。
contradictory accountsで「食い違う・矛盾する証言」。
items.translation: 2人の目撃者が事故について食い違う証言をしたため、警察は近くの防犯カメラを確認しなければなりませんでした。

items.prompt: Regular exercise can help (     ) the negative effects of sitting at a desk all day.
items.explanation: 一日中机に座っていることによる悪影響を定期的な運動が「打ち消す・相殺する」のでcounteract。
distractorReasons: counteractは「悪影響などを打ち消す、中和する」。
exaggerateは「誇張する」。
cultivateは「耕す、育む」でnegative effectsを目的語にしない。
prosecuteは「起訴する」。
items.translation: 定期的な運動は一日中デスクに座っていることによる悪影響を打ち消す助けになります。

items.prompt: The airline offered meal vouchers to passengers as (     ) for the five-hour flight delay.
items.explanation: 5時間の便遅延に対する「補償・おわび」として食事券を提供したのでcompensation。

items.prompt: Although the new battery is slightly heavier, its capacity is (     ) superior to that of the previous model.

items.translation: 新しいバッテリーはわずかに重くなっていますが、その容量は前のモデルよりはるかに優れています。

items.prompt: Dr. Patel's lecture was so technical that most first-year students could not (     ) her main point.

items.prompt: The small publishing house managed to stay afloat (     ) a series of popular children's science books.
items.explanation: 人気の児童向け科学書シリーズ「のおかげで」経営を維持できたのでby virtue ofを選ぶ。

items.prompt: Only after the audit report was released (     ) how much money had been wasted.
items.explanation: Only＋副詞節（Only after ...）が文頭に出たため、主節が疑問文語順（助動詞did＋主語＋原形）に倒置される。

inheritは「受け継ぐ」。

items.prompt: The software update will take effect automatically unless users choose to opt (     ) beforehand.
items.explanation: 事前に適用除外を選ばない限り自動更新される。opt outで「不参加を選ぶ、離脱する」。

items.prompt: Had it not been for the lighthouse keeper's quick warning, the fishing boat (     ) the rocks.
items.explanation: Had it not been for ...（もし〜がなかったら）は過去の仮定法過去完了の条件節なので、主節はwould have＋過去分詞。

items.prompt: The research team decided to (     ) with the outdated survey method and design a clearer questionnaire.
items.explanation: 時代遅れの調査手法を「廃止して」より明確な質問票を作ることにしたのでdo away withを選ぶ。

do away with ...で「〜を廃止する、取り除く」。
come up withは「（案などを）思いつく」。
get along withは「〜と仲良くやる」。
items.translation: 研究チームは時代遅れの調査手法を廃止し、より明確なアンケートを設計することに決めました。

items.prompt: Participation in Saturday's beach cleanup is entirely (     ); nobody will be penalized for not attending.
items.explanation: 欠席しても一切不利益がないことから、土曜の海岸清掃への参加は完全に「任意の・自発的な」もの。

voluntaryは「任意の、自発的な」。
inevitableは「避けられない」。
unanimousは「満場一致の」。
items.translation: 土曜日の海岸清掃への参加は完全に任意であり、不参加でも不利益を受けることはありません。

passage.title: Why Hospital Signs Stopped Using Medical Department Names
passage.text:
Large hospitals can be intimidating places to navigate, especially for anxious patients arriving for the first time. Traditionally, corridor signs directed visitors using formal medical terms such as "Otolaryngology," "Nephrology," or "Ophthalmology." To doctors and nurses, these names were precise and unambiguous. To many patients and family members, however, the unfamiliar Latin and Greek words slowed them down and forced them to stop staff in hallways for directions.

When a regional medical center renovated its main building, a communication researcher observed visitors at the entrance desk for two weeks. Nearly forty percent of inquiries came from people who already held appointment slips yet could not match the technical department name to everyday language. The hospital had inadvertently designed its signs for people who already worked there rather than for (18).

During the redesign, planners replaced complex terminology on main hallway signs with plain descriptions such as "Ear, Nose & Throat," "Kidney Care," and "Eye Clinic," accompanied by numbered color bands along the walls. Specialist terms were still printed in smaller letters underneath so medical referrals remained exact. (19), nurses spent far less time giving basic directions, and fewer patients arrived late for appointments.

The project demonstrated that accuracy and clarity need not conflict. Keeping technical terms on medical records while using everyday words on public signs allowed the hospital to (20).
passage.translation: 大病院は初めて訪れる不安な患者にとって迷いやすい場所だ。従来、院内の案内表示には「耳鼻咽喉科」「腎臓内科」「眼科」に相当する難解なラテン語・ギリシャ語由来の正式医学名称が使われてきた。医師や看護師には正確でも、多くの患者や家族にはなじみが薄く、廊下で職員を呼び止めて道を尋ねる原因になっていた。ある地域医療センターが本館を改修した際、研究者が受付を2週間観察したところ、質問の約4割は予約票を持っているのに専門診療科名と日常語が結びつかない人からのものだった。病院は無意識のうちに、(18)ではなく院内で働く人向けに標識を作っていたのだ。再設計では主廊下の表示を「耳・鼻・のど」「腎臓ケア」「目のクリニック」といった平易な表現と色分け番号帯に改め、紹介状との照合用に正式名称を小さく併記した。(19)、看護師が道案内に費やす時間は大幅に減り、予約に遅れる患者も減少した。診療記録の専門性と館内表示の分かりやすさを両立させたこの取り組みは、病院が(20)ことを可能にしたのである。

passage.title: Planting Pocket Forests in Industrial Districts
passage.text:
Urban tree-planting campaigns often place single young trees at regular intervals along concrete sidewalks. While tidy in appearance, isolated street trees frequently struggle in compacted soil, suffer from heat reflected off asphalt, and grow slowly. In paved industrial districts where summer temperatures rise sharply, planners have begun testing an alternative approach known as "pocket forests."

Instead of spacing one species evenly along a curb, landscapers loosen a plot of soil no larger than a tennis court, enrich it with compost, and plant dozens of native tree and shrub species close together. Because the young plants compete gently for sunlight while shading the soil beneath them, moisture evaporates more slowly and roots establish themselves rapidly. Within three years, a dense multi-layered canopy can form, creating (21).

Critics initially questioned whether tiny plots could make any measurable difference beside busy warehouses. Temperature sensors installed by university researchers showed that air directly inside and downwind of the pocket forests was several degrees cooler on summer afternoons than surrounding parking lots. (22), factory workers began using benches beside the plots during lunch breaks, and songbirds returned to areas where they had rarely been seen.

Planners emphasize that pocket forests are not a substitute for large suburban parks, which offer sports fields and long walking trails. Rather, their strength lies in (23) where large expanses of open land are simply unavailable.
passage.translation: 都市の植樹事業ではコンクリートの歩道沿いに単一種の若木を等間隔に植えることが多い。見た目は整っていても、孤立した街路樹は踏み固められた土壌やアスファルトの照り返しに苦しみ成長も遅い。夏の気温が急上昇する舗装だらけの工業地区では、「ポケット・フォレスト（小さな森）」と呼ばれる別手法の試験が始まっている。縁石沿いに1種ずつ離して植える代わりに、テニスコートほどの区画の土をほぐして堆肥を混ぜ、数十種の在来樹木や低木を密植する。若木同士が日光を求めて適度に競い合い足元の土に影を作るため、水分の蒸発が抑えられ根が素早く張る。3年以内に多層の樹冠が茂り、(21)を生み出す。当初は倉庫街の小さな区画に効果があるのか疑問視する声もあったが、大学研究者の温度計は夏の午後に区画内や風下の気温が周辺駐車場より数度低いことを示した。(22)、工場で働く人々が昼休みに横のベンチを使い始め、めったに見られなかった野鳥も戻ってきた。計画担当者は、運動場や長い遊歩道を備える郊外の大公園に取って代わるものではなく、広い土地が確保できない場所で(23)点にこそ強みがあると強調する。

passage.title: Planting Pocket Forests in Industrial Districts
passage.text:
Urban tree-planting campaigns often place single young trees at regular intervals along concrete sidewalks. While tidy in appearance, isolated street trees frequently struggle in compacted soil, suffer from heat reflected off asphalt, and grow slowly. Instead of spacing one species evenly along a curb, landscapers loosen a plot of soil no larger than a tennis court, enrich it with compost, and plant dozens of native tree and shrub species close together. Because the young plants compete gently for sunlight while shading the soil beneath them, moisture evaporates more slowly and roots establish themselves rapidly. Within three years, a dense multi-layered canopy can form, creating (21).

Critics initially questioned whether tiny plots could make any measurable difference beside busy warehouses. Temperature sensors installed by university researchers showed that air directly inside and downwind of the pocket forests was several degrees cooler on summer afternoons than surrounding parking lots. (22), factory workers began using benches beside the plots during lunch breaks, and songbirds returned to areas where they had rarely been seen.

passage.title: Notice Regarding the Archive Digitization Project
passage.text:
From: Marcus Vance, Head Archivist
To: Part-Time Scanning Assistants
Subject: Updated procedures for the newspaper collection

Dear assistants,
Thank you for your steady work digitizing our nineteenth-century town newspapers. Over the past month, our online archive has already been used by local high schools and historical researchers. As we move on to the older 1870–1885 volumes next Monday, we need to adjust two workflow rules to protect fragile paper.

First, please stop using the automatic sheet feeder completely. Even single pages from the 1870s are brittle along the margins and may tear if pulled by rollers. Every page must be placed by hand onto the overhead flatbed camera. This will reduce the number of pages scanned per hour, so we have removed the daily page target that applied last month. Quality and preservation take priority over speed.

Second, when an article contains faded ink that optical software cannot read reliably, please mark the file with the tag "MANUAL-CHECK" rather than guessing the missing words yourself. Our senior historians will review flagged pages every Thursday.

White cotton gloves turned out to reduce finger sensitivity and actually caused more accidental creases, so please wash and dry your hands thoroughly before each shift instead of wearing gloves. Let me know if you need training on the overhead camera before Monday.

Sincerely,
Marcus Vance
passage.translation: 差出人マーカス・ヴァンス（主任アーキビスト）、宛先スキャン補助スタッフ各位、件名：新聞コレクションの作業手順変更について。19世紀の町内新聞デジタル化への着実な取り組みに感謝。先月来すでに地元高校や歴史研究者に活用されている。来週月曜からさらに古い1870〜1885年分の冊子に入るため、もろい紙を保護する目的で手順を2点変更する。第1に、自動原稿送り装置の使用を全面中止すること。1870年代の紙は端がもろくローラーで破れる恐れがあるため、全ページを手作業で上向きフラットベッドカメラに置くこと。時間あたりの枚数は減るため、先月設けていた1日の枚数目標は撤廃した（速度より品質と保存を優先）。第2に、インクのかすれで文字認識ソフトが正確に読めない箇所は、自分で推測して補わず「MANUAL-CHECK」タグを付けること（毎週木曜に専門研究員が確認する）。また白い綿手袋は指先の感覚を鈍らせかえって折り目を作る原因になったため、手袋は着用せずシフト前に手洗いと乾燥を徹底すること。月曜前にカメラ研修が必要なら連絡してほしい。

passage.title: Rethinking How Cities Measure Bus Punctuality
passage.text:
Most city bus networks judge their performance by a familiar standard: whether each bus arrives at stops at the exact minute printed on the timetable. On quiet suburban routes that run twice an hour, this measure makes complete sense. Missing the 9:10 bus means waiting thirty minutes in the cold, so passengers check the clock before leaving home.

On busy urban corridors where buses are scheduled every five or six minutes, however, passengers behave differently. Commuters rarely consult a timetable; they simply walk to the stop expecting a bus to appear shortly. Yet heavy traffic frequently causes a frustrating pattern known as "bus bunching." If one bus is delayed for ninety seconds by a delivery van, slightly more passengers gather at the next stop. Boarding takes longer, delaying that bus further, while the following bus encounters almost empty stops and catches up. Soon two or three buses travel nose to tail, followed by a fifteen-minute gap.

Curiously, under traditional punctuality rules, an operator could try to keep drivers tied to fixed clock times even after traffic disrupted the pattern, or penalize drivers who paused briefly to restore spacing. When transit planners in Harborview analyzed passenger complaints, they realized riders on high-frequency routes did not care which specific bus they boarded; they cared about how long they waited on the sidewalk.

Harborview subsequently switched its evaluation of six-minute routes from timetable adherence to "headway regularity"—keeping the time interval between consecutive buses steady. Dispatchers gained authority to ask an ahead-of-schedule bus to wait forty seconds at a transfer hub so a gap would not widen downstream. Digital signs at stops also began showing "Every 6 minutes" alongside live countdowns rather than long lists of clock times.

Average waiting times fell by nearly twenty percent without adding extra vehicles or drivers. Nevertheless, transit specialists note that headway management works only when routes are frequent and dispatchers communicate clearly with passengers on board; nobody likes sitting at a stop for forty seconds unless the driver explains why. Choosing the right metric, they conclude, depends on matching measurement to how passengers actually experience a journey.
passage.translation: 多くの都市バス網は「時刻表通りの分に各停留所へ到着したか」で運行成績を評価している。1時間に2本の静かな郊外路線ではこの指標は極めて合理的だ。9時10分の便を逃せば寒い中30分待つため、乗客は時計を見て家を出る。しかし5〜6分間隔で走る都市部の幹線では乗客の行動が異なる。乗客は時刻表を見ず、すぐ来るだろうと停留所へ向かう。ところが混雑した道路では「団子運転（バス・バンチング）」が頻発する。1台が配送車で90秒遅れると次の停留所で乗客が増え、乗車に時間がかかってさらに遅れる一方、後続便は空いた停留所を素早く通過して追いつき、2〜3台が続行した後に15分の空白が生じるのだ。奇妙なことに従来の定時性基準では間隔調整のための小休止が減点対象にさえなり得た。ハーバービュー市の交通計画担当者が苦情を分析すると、高頻度路線の乗客が気にしているのは「どの便に乗れたか」ではなく「歩道で何分待ったか」だった。そこで同市は6分間隔路線の評価基準を時刻表順守から「運行間隔の均等性」へ切り替え、先行しすぎた便に乗換拠点で40秒待機して後続との間隔を保つ指示を出せるようにした。車両や運転手を増やさずに平均待ち時間は約20％短縮された。もっとも専門家は、この手法が高頻度路線かつ車内放送での丁寧な理由説明とセットで初めて機能すると指摘し、乗客の実際の利用体験に合った指標選びの重要性を結論づけている。

passage.title: Rethinking How Cities Measure Bus Punctuality
passage.text:
Most city bus networks judge their performance by a familiar standard: whether each bus arrives at stops at the exact minute printed on the timetable. On quiet suburban routes that run twice an hour, this measure makes complete sense. Missing the 9:10 bus means waiting thirty minutes in the cold, so passengers check the clock before leaving home.

On busy urban corridors where buses are scheduled every five or six minutes, however, passengers behave differently. Commuters rarely consult a timetable; they simply walk to the stop expecting a bus to appear shortly. Yet heavy traffic frequently causes a frustrating pattern known as "bus bunching." If one bus is delayed for ninety seconds by a delivery van, slightly more passengers gather at the next stop. Boarding takes longer, delaying that bus further, while the following bus encounters almost empty stops and catches up. Soon two or three buses travel nose to tail, followed by a fifteen-minute gap.

Curiously, under traditional punctuality rules, an operator could try to keep drivers tied to fixed clock times even after traffic disrupted the pattern, or penalize drivers who paused briefly to restore spacing. When transit planners in Harborview analyzed passenger complaints, they realized riders on high-frequency routes did not care which specific bus they boarded; they cared about how long they waited on the sidewalk.

Harborview subsequently switched its evaluation of six-minute routes from timetable adherence to "headway regularity"—keeping the time interval between consecutive buses steady. Dispatchers gained authority to ask an ahead-of-schedule bus to wait forty seconds at a transfer hub so a gap would not widen downstream. Digital signs at stops also began showing "Every 6 minutes" alongside live countdowns rather than long lists of clock times.

Average waiting times fell by nearly twenty percent without adding extra vehicles or drivers. Nevertheless, transit specialists note that headway management works only when routes are frequent and dispatchers communicate clearly with passengers on board; nobody likes sitting at a stop for forty seconds unless the driver explains why. Choosing the right metric, they conclude, depends on matching measurement to how passengers actually experience a journey.
passage.translation: 多くの都市バス網は「時刻表通りの分に各停留所へ到着したか」で運行成績を評価している。1時間に2本の静かな郊外路線ではこの指標は極めて合理的だ。9時10分の便を逃せば寒い中30分待つため、乗客は時計を見て家を出る。しかし5〜6分間隔で走る都市部の幹線では乗客の行動が異なる。乗客は時刻表を見ず、すぐ来るだろうと停留所へ向かう。ところが混雑した道路では「団子運転（バス・バンチング）」が頻発する。1台が配送車で90秒遅れると次の停留所で乗客が増え、乗車に時間がかかってさらに遅れる一方、後続便は空いた停留所を素早く通過して追いつき、2〜3台が続行した後に15分の空白が生じるのだ。奇妙なことに従来の定時性基準では間隔調整のための小休止が減点対象にさえなり得た。ハーバービュー市の交通計画担当者が苦情を分析すると、高頻度路線の乗客が気にしているのは「どの便に乗れたか」ではなく「歩道で何分待ったか」だった。そこで同市は6分間隔路線の評価基準を時刻表順守から「運行間隔の均等性」へ切り替え、先行しすぎた便に乗換拠点で40秒待機して後続との間隔を保つ指示を出せるようにした。車両や運転手を増やさずに平均待ち時間は約20％短縮された。もっとも専門家は、この手法が高頻度路線かつ車内放送での丁寧な理由説明とセットで初めて機能すると指摘し、乗客の実際の利用体験に合った指標選びの重要性を結論づけている。

items.prompt: What did switching to "headway regularity" achieve in Harborview?

It cut average passenger waiting times by nearly twenty percent with existing buses.

items.translation: 「運行間隔の均等性」への切り替えはハーバービュー市でどんな成果を上げましたか。

items.prompt: According to the final paragraph, why is clear communication with onboard passengers necessary?
choices: So passengers understand why a bus pauses briefly to balance spacing.
So passengers can drive the bus themselves at transfer hubs.

items.prompt: 以下の英文を読んで、その内容を英語で要約し、解答欄に記入しなさい。本文にない自分の意見は加えないこと。（目安語数：45〜55語）

passage.title: Returning Packaging Through Local Delivery Vans
passage.text:
As online shopping continues to grow, households receive millions of cardboard boxes and protective plastic cushions every week. Although cardboard can often be recycled through municipal collection, bulky packing materials quickly fill household bins, and manufacturing single-use boxes consumes considerable water and timber.

To address this issue, several delivery companies have begun testing reusable folding containers made of durable lightweight plastic. When a driver delivers a new order to an apartment building, customers can hand back flattened containers from previous deliveries so the van carries them back on its return trip.

However, the system faces practical challenges. Storing empty containers requires warehouse space, and some customers forget to return them promptly. To encourage timely returns, participating retailers now offer small shipping discounts whenever a container is scanned back at the door.
passage.translation:
ネット通販の拡大に伴い、各家庭には毎週膨大な段ボール箱や緩衝材が届いている。段ボールは自治体の回収でリサイクルできることが多いものの、かさばる梱包材は家庭のごみ箱をすぐに埋め、使い捨て箱の製造には大量の水や木材が消費される。
この問題に対処するため、複数の配送会社が丈夫で軽いプラスチック製の折りたたみ式通い箱の試験を始めた。配達員が集合住宅へ新しい荷物を届ける際、客が前回の箱をたたんで返却すれば帰りの便で回収できる。
しかし課題もある。空箱の保管には倉庫面積が要り、返却を忘れる客もいる。そこで参加小売店は、玄関先で箱の返却スキャンが完了するたびに少額の送料割引を提供して早期返却を促している。

items.model: Growing online shopping creates bulky packaging waste and consumes natural resources. Consequently, several delivery companies are testing reusable folding containers collected from customers during later deliveries. However, storing empty containers requires warehouse space and customers sometimes forget to return them, so participating retailers offer small shipping discounts to encourage prompt returns.
items.translation: 拡大するネット通販はかさばる梱包ごみを生み天然資源を消費する。そのため複数の配送会社は次回配達時に客から回収する再利用可能な折りたたみ容器を試している。しかし空箱の保管には倉庫面積が必要で客が返却を忘れることもあるため、参加小売店は少額の送料割引を行って迅速な返却を促している。
items.explanation: 第1段落の背景（通販拡大に伴う梱包ごみと資源消費）、第2段落の取り組み（次回配達時に回収する折りたたみ再利用容器）、第3段落の課題と対策（倉庫面積や返却忘れに対し送料割引で促進）を51語で過不足なく要約しています。
rubric: 通販の拡大に伴う梱包材廃棄・資源消費の背景を示した
折りたたみ式再利用容器の配達時回収の仕組みを含めた
保管場所・返却忘れの課題と送料割引による対策を結んだ
自分の意見を加えず45〜55語の目安に収めた

items.prompt:
次のTOPICについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ書きなさい。POINTSは理由を書く際の参考として自由に用いてかまいません。（目安語数：80〜100語）
TOPIC: Today, some museums allow visitors to take photographs of exhibits without flash. Do you think more museums should adopt this policy?
POINTS:
• Education
• Promotion
• Manners
items.model:
I think more museums should allow visitors to take photographs of exhibits without using flash.
First, photographs are valuable for education. Visitors often see hundreds of historical objects during a single visit and cannot remember every detail. Reviewing their own pictures at home helps students and researchers deepen their understanding.
Second, visitor photos serve as effective promotion. When people share favorite exhibits with friends or online, more young people become interested in visiting museums in person.
As long as quiet manners are enforced, flash-free photography benefits both visitors and museums.
items.translation:
私はより多くの博物館や美術館が、フラッシュを使わない展示物の写真撮影を来館者に認めるべきだと思います。
第一に、写真は教育面で有益です。来館者は1回の訪問で何百もの歴史的資料を目にするため細部まで覚えきれませんが、帰宅後に自分の写真を見返せば生徒や研究者は理解を深められます。
第二に、来館者の写真は効果的な広報になります。お気に入りの展示を友人やネット上で共有すれば、実際に足を運びたいと思う若者が増えます。
静かに鑑賞するマナーが守られる限り、フラッシュなしの撮影は来館者と施設の双方に利益をもたらします。
items.explanation: POINTSのEducationとPromotionを軸に、結論でMannersの条件も自然に添えて90語で論理的に構成しています。
rubric: 賛否の立場を冒頭で明確に示した
教育効果・広報効果など2つの異なる理由を具体的に展開した
語彙・構文を適切に使い段落構成を整えた
80〜100語の目安に収まっている

imminentは差し迫った。

passage.title: The Silence in the Archive
passage.text:
Historical collections are sometimes treated as though they were transparent windows onto the past. A researcher asks a question, locates the relevant papers, and extracts an answer. Yet the existence of a document reflects a chain of decisions: someone had to produce it, someone had to retain it, and an institution eventually had to consider it worth preserving. Groups whose daily activities generated few written records may consequently be difficult to study, even when their contribution to a community was substantial.

Consider a project reconstructing the history of a neighborhood market. Official files might contain detailed records of licenses and inspections, while offering almost nothing about informal arrangements through which traders shared transport or helped a sick colleague. If researchers relied exclusively on official files, they could (19). What was easiest to document would acquire disproportionate importance simply because it had survived in an accessible form.

Oral interviews can help broaden such a project, but they do not provide an uncomplicated solution. People may interpret earlier experiences through the concerns of the present. Different accounts may disagree without either speaker deliberately misleading the interviewer. (20), recordings should be accompanied by information about when and under what circumstances they were made. This enables later users to assess the accounts instead of treating them as context-free statements.

An honest archive therefore makes its own limitations visible. It can identify gaps, explain selection policies, and preserve disagreements rather than forcing every account into a single version of events. This does not make historical research impossible. On the contrary, recognizing how a collection was assembled allows researchers to (21). The aim is not to abandon evidence but to ask more precise questions of it.
passage.translation: 歴史資料は過去をそのまま映す窓ではありません。作成、保管、収蔵の各段階で選択があり、書面を残しにくい集団は貢献が大きくても調べにくくなります。市場の歴史を公文書だけで再構成すると許認可や検査は詳しくても、輸送の共有や病気の仲間への援助など非公式な実務が見えず、(19)おそれがあります。口述は範囲を広げますが、現在の関心による記憶の解釈や、故意でない不一致もあります。(20)、録音には日時と状況を付記して、後の利用者が文脈を評価できるようにすべきです。資料館は欠落や選定方針を示し、不一致も保存すべきです。これは研究を不可能にするのでなく、収集の過程を認識することで研究者が(21)のを可能にします。証拠を捨てるのでなく、より精確に問うことが目的です。

passage.title: A Standard Is Not a Setting
passage.text:
When a public agency purchases a digital service, adopting a technical standard can appear to resolve the question of accessibility. A supplier certifies that its product complies, the certificate is filed, and the agency proceeds with installation. Standards are indispensable because they establish common expectations that would otherwise have to be negotiated separately for every purchase. However, a certificate describes a product under specified conditions, not every future interaction between that product and its users.

Imagine a booking system that works correctly when tested in isolation. During installation, an agency adds a short time limit, requires documents available only as scanned images, and places essential instructions on another website. Each decision may seem administratively convenient. Taken together, they can create obstacles that were absent from the original test. A compliant product has not necessarily produced (22).

User testing after installation is therefore essential, but it must be organized carefully. Inviting only experienced staff to complete familiar tasks is unlikely to reveal the difficulties faced by someone using assistive technology or encountering the process for the first time. Agencies need feedback from people whose circumstances differ, and a procedure for acting on that feedback. (23), collecting complaints without assigning responsibility for resolving them merely documents exclusion rather than reducing it.

This does not mean that technical standards should be discarded. They provide a necessary baseline and make suppliers accountable for features within their control. The problem arises when meeting a baseline is treated as the end of the agency's responsibility. Accessibility is sustained through procurement, configuration, testing, and maintenance. An effective approach consequently requires agencies to (24), rather than regard accessibility as a property that can be purchased once and then forgotten.
passage.translation: 行政のデジタルサービス調達では、技術標準への適合証明でアクセシビリティ問題が解決したように見えがちです。標準は共通の期待を定めるため不可欠ですが、証明は特定条件下の製品についてで、将来の全利用場面を保証しません。単体試験では正常な予約システムも、導入時に短い制限時間、画像だけの書類、別サイトの重要な説明を加えると障壁を生みます。適合製品が必ずしも(22)を生むわけではありません。導入後の試験も熟練職員だけでは不十分で、支援技術利用者や初回利用者など異なる事情の人の意見と、それに対処する手順が必要です。(23)、解決責任を割り当てず苦情を集めるだけでは排除を記録するにとどまります。標準を廃棄すべきなのでなく、最低基準達成を責任の終点としないことが重要です。調達、設定、試験、保守を通じて(24)必要があります。

passage.title: Who Benefits from a Quieter Street?
passage.text:
Reducing traffic on a residential street may seem an uncomplicated improvement. Fewer vehicles can mean less noise, cleaner air, and more space for people walking or cycling. Yet the evaluation of a traffic scheme depends on where its boundaries are drawn. A street that becomes quieter may sit beside another that receives the diverted vehicles. An assessment limited to the first street can therefore tell a convincing but incomplete story.

Suppose a district introduces barriers that prevent through-traffic from using several residential roads. Initial monitoring shows a sharp decline in vehicles inside the area. Residents living near the barriers report that children can cross more easily and that conversations are no longer interrupted by engine noise. These are genuine benefits, not merely perceptions to be dismissed. However, residents along the main roads outside the area report longer queues. They question why their experience is absent from the first evaluation.

One response is to enlarge the monitoring area. This is necessary, but a larger average alone may still obscure important differences. If a substantial improvement for several thousand people outweighs a smaller deterioration for a few hundred, the overall figure may look favorable. That calculation does not by itself establish whether the distribution of costs is acceptable, especially if those facing deterioration already experience the greatest pollution. Choosing a measurement boundary is therefore not a neutral substitute for considering fairness.

Timing introduces another complication. Drivers may initially follow familiar routes and later change their journey, travel at another hour, or choose another means of transport. The first week may consequently exaggerate permanent disruption. Conversely, waiting for people to adapt cannot justify disregarding persistent problems indefinitely. An evaluation should state in advance when it will be repeated and which findings would trigger a change. Otherwise, every unfavorable result can be described as temporary and every favorable result as final.

A credible process combines measurements with ways for affected people to challenge the interpretation. Residents may identify a school entrance that monitors have missed or explain why a supposedly convenient alternative route is unusable for someone with limited mobility. Their accounts do not replace traffic counts, but they can reveal what the counts fail to capture.

The choice is not simply between accepting every scheme and rejecting any scheme with uneven effects. It is between treating evaluation as a defense of a completed decision and using it to revise that decision. A project can retain its original aims while adding protection for neighboring roads, adjusting delivery access, or removing a barrier that causes disproportionate harm. A quieter street is worth pursuing, but the claim of success becomes stronger when it accounts for people beyond that street.
passage.translation: 住宅街の交通量削減には騒音や空気、歩行環境の改善がありますが、迂回車を受ける周辺道路を評価に含めなければ不完全です。通過交通を防ぐ障壁によって内側の住民は実際に恩恵を受けても、外側の幹線道路の渋滞は最初の評価に表れないことがあります。測定範囲を広げても、平均値は大多数の改善で少数者の悪化を隠しえます。すでに高い汚染にさらされた人に費用が集中する場合、公平さは平均だけで決められません。導入直後と経路・時間・交通手段が適応した後でも結果は異なりますが、適応を口実に永続的な問題を無視することはできません。再評価時期と変更条件を事前に示す必要があります。住民は見落とされた学校入口や移動困難者には使えない代替路を指摘できます。体験談は交通量計測を置き換えず、欠落を発見します。評価は既決定の弁護でなく改善に使うべきで、隣接道路の保護、配送経路の調整、不均衡な害を生む障壁の撤去などで当初の目的を保ちながら修正できます。静かな街路の成功は、その外側の人も考慮するとき、より説得力を持ちます。

Yet the evaluation of a traffic scheme depends on where its boundaries are drawn. A street that becomes quieter may sit beside another that receives the diverted vehicles. An assessment limited to the first street can therefore tell a convincing but incomplete story.

Suppose a district introduces barriers that prevent through-traffic from using several residential roads. Initial monitoring shows a sharp decline in vehicles inside the area. Residents living near the barriers report that children can cross more easily and that conversations are no longer interrupted by engine noise. These are genuine benefits, not merely perceptions to be dismissed. However, residents along the main roads outside the area report longer queues. They question why their experience is absent from the first evaluation.

One response is to enlarge the monitoring area. This is necessary, but a larger average alone may still obscure important differences. If a substantial improvement for several thousand people outweighs a smaller deterioration for a few hundred, the overall figure may look favorable. That calculation does not by itself establish whether the distribution of costs is acceptable, especially if those facing deterioration already experience the greatest pollution. Choosing a measurement boundary is therefore not a neutral substitute for considering fairness.

Timing introduces another complication. Drivers may initially follow familiar routes and later change their journey, travel at another hour, or choose another means of transport. The first week may consequently exaggerate permanent disruption. Conversely, waiting for people to adapt cannot justify disregarding persistent problems indefinitely. An evaluation should state in advance when it will be repeated and which findings would trigger a change. Otherwise, every unfavorable result can be described as temporary and every favorable result as final.

A credible process combines measurements with ways for affected people to challenge the interpretation. Residents may identify a school entrance that monitors have missed or explain why a supposedly convenient alternative route is unusable for someone with limited mobility. Their accounts do not replace traffic counts, but they can reveal what the counts fail to capture.

The choice is not simply between accepting every scheme and rejecting any scheme with uneven effects. It is between treating evaluation as a defense of a completed decision and using it to revise that decision. A project can retain its original aims while adding protection for neighboring roads, adjusting delivery access, or removing a barrier that causes disproportionate harm. A quieter street is worth pursuing, but the claim of success becomes stronger when it accounts for people beyond that street.

passage.title: Learning from a Pilot Without Copying It
passage.text:
A successful pilot project is often presented as a miniature version of a future policy. If a service works for a small group, expanding it appears to be a matter of securing enough money and reproducing the same arrangement elsewhere. This picture is appealing to decision-makers because it turns uncertainty into an apparently manageable problem of scale. Unfortunately, the conditions that make a pilot succeed may be precisely those that cannot be reproduced simply by increasing its budget.

Consider a pilot designed to help residents navigate complicated housing applications. A small team operates from a familiar community center, and its coordinator has long-standing relationships with both local families and officials. Staff can telephone a particular official to clarify an unusual case, and residents who distrust formal agencies may approach the coordinator because a neighbor recommends her. None of these features is captured by a description that says only "advice provided at a local center."

When the service is expanded, new offices may be established quickly, but relationships take time. The original coordinator may also have exercised considerable judgment about which rules could be interpreted flexibly and which required strict compliance. A standardized handbook can preserve some of this knowledge, but not necessarily the ability to recognize a new situation. If policymakers copy only the visible procedure, they may reproduce its appearance while losing the mechanisms that made it effective.

This does not render pilots useless. Rather, it changes what should be learned from them. Evaluation needs to identify not only whether an outcome improved but also how the improvement occurred. Were staff reducing delays because they simplified paperwork, because they knew whom to contact, or because the pilot received exceptional attention from senior officials? These explanations imply different prospects for expansion. A process that depends on an unusual level of senior attention may be harder to sustain than one based on a broadly applicable change in application forms.

There is also a danger in selecting only the most enthusiastic communities for a pilot and then treating their results as representative. Such communities may contribute unpaid labor, adapt buildings, or solve problems informally. These contributions can be legitimate strengths of the pilot, but they should not disappear from the account of its costs. Expansion to areas without the same resources may require additional funding or a different design.

A useful next step may therefore be a deliberately varied second trial, rather than immediate nationwide adoption. This trial can test the service in places with different staffing, relationships, and levels of local support. Some adaptations should be permitted, provided the essential mechanism and the reason for each change are documented. Uniformity of every visible detail is not the same as fidelity to the project's purpose.

Ultimately, the most responsible claim for a pilot is rarely that it has eliminated uncertainty. It has made certain assumptions more testable and exposed conditions that deserve attention. Policymakers can then decide which elements should be preserved, which require investment, and which must change. Scaling a project intelligently is a process of learning across settings, not transporting a finished object from one place to another.
passage.translation: 小規模実証の成功を、資金を増やせばそのまま大規模化できる政策の縮図と見るのは危険です。住宅申請を助ける仮の事業では、地域の信頼や職員との長年の関係、例外への判断力が成果を生んでいるかもしれません。「地域センターで助言」という手順だけではそれらを捉えられません。新窓口や手引書を増やしても、関係や新しい事例の判断力は直ちに複製できません。実証は無用なのではなく、結果だけでなく作用の仕組みを調べる必要があります。書類の簡素化、連絡先の知識、幹部の特別な注目のどれが遅延を減らしたかで拡張の見通しは異なります。熱心な地域だけを選ぶと無償労働や施設改修、非公式な解決能力が見落とされ、通常地域には追加費用や設計変更が必要になりえます。すぐ全国導入せず、多様な条件で2段階目の試験を行う方が有用な場合があります。本質的な仕組みと変更理由を記録すれば適応を許すべきで、外見の一律性と目的への忠実さは同じではありません。実証の価値は不確実性の消滅でなく、前提の検証可能性と注意すべき条件の発見にあります。賢い拡張とは完成品の移送でなく、異なる場で学ぶ過程です。

items.prompt: 以下の英文を読んで、その内容を英語で要約し、解答欄に記入しなさい。本文にない自分の意見は加えないこと。（目安語数：60〜70語）

passage.title: Adaptive Reuse of Industrial Buildings
passage.text:
Across many cities, former factories and warehouses stand vacant after manufacturing moves elsewhere. Instead of demolishing these structures and constructing entirely new buildings, urban planners increasingly favor adaptive reuse—converting existing industrial shells into housing, libraries, or offices. Preserving structural frames substantially reduces demolition waste and avoids the carbon emissions associated with producing new concrete and steel. Reused landmarks can also help neighborhoods retain their distinctive architectural character.

Nevertheless, adaptive reuse is far from effortless. Older industrial buildings rarely satisfy contemporary standards for thermal insulation, fire safety, or wheelchair access. Developers frequently uncover hidden structural deterioration or hazardous materials once renovation begins, causing budgets and schedules to overrun.

Specialists therefore emphasize thorough preliminary inspections before a conversion is approved, alongside building regulations flexible enough to accommodate historic structures without compromising essential safety.
passage.translation:
多くの都市で製造業の移転後に旧工場や倉庫が空いたまま残っている。都市計画家はこれらを取り壊して新築する代わりに、既存の産業建築の躯体を住宅や図書館、オフィスへ転用する「アダプティブ・リユース（転用改修）」を支持するようになっている。構造躯体の保存は解体廃棄物を大幅に減らし、新たなコンクリートや鋼材の製造に伴う炭素排出も抑えられる。象徴的な建物を再利用することで地域固有の建築的個性も保てる。
しかし転用改修は決して容易ではない。古い産業建築は現代の断熱・防火・バリアフリー基準を満たさないことが多い。改修開始後に隠れた構造劣化や有害物質が見つかり、予算や工期を超過する例も少なくない。
そのため専門家は、転用承認前の綿密な事前調査と、不可欠な安全性を損なわずに歴史的建造物へ対応できる柔軟な建築規制の重要性を強調している。

items.model: Converting vacant industrial buildings into new public or residential facilities significantly reduces demolition waste and carbon emissions while preserving local architectural heritage. However, renovating older structures often involves unexpected expenses and delays due to strict modern standards, hidden structural damage, and hazardous materials. Consequently, experts recommend comprehensive inspections beforehand and flexible building regulations that maintain essential safety while accommodating historic designs.
items.translation: 空いた産業建築を新たな施設へ転用することは、地域の建築遺産を守りつつ解体廃棄物と炭素排出を減らす。しかし古い建物の改修では、厳格な現代基準や隠れた構造損傷、有害物質のために予想外の費用や遅れが生じやすい。そのため専門家は、綿密な事前調査と、安全性を保ちつつ歴史的構造に対応できる柔軟な建築規則を推奨している。
items.explanation: 第1段落の利点（廃棄物・炭素排出削減と地域景観の維持）、第2段落の課題（現代基準への適合難・隠れた劣化や有害物質による費用と工期の超過）、第3段落の提言（事前調査の徹底と安全性を担保した柔軟な規制）を60〜70語（56語だと不足するため厳密調整済みの60語以上）でパラフレーズしています。
rubric: 転用改修の環境面・景観面の利点を自分の言葉で要約した
現代基準・構造劣化・有害物質に伴うコストや遅延の課題を含めた
専門家が求める事前調査と柔軟な規制の必要性を正確に結んだ
主観を交えず60〜70語の厳格な語数範囲に収めた

items.prompt:
次のTOPICについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ書きなさい。POINTSから2つを選び、序論・本論（2つ）・結論の構成で論述しなさい。（目安語数：120〜150語）
TOPIC: Should governments provide financial incentives for people to move from major cities to rural areas?
POINTS:
• Cost of living
• Employment opportunities
• Local public services
• Infrastructure maintenance
items.model:
I believe governments should provide financial incentives to encourage residents of major cities to relocate to rural communities.
First, such support helps sustain local public services. Many rural towns face rapid population decline, forcing schools, clinics, and bus routes to close. Attracting working-age families increases local tax revenue and demand, making it viable for municipalities to maintain essential services for all residents.
Second, relocation incentives ease the high cost of living experienced in overcrowded metropolitan areas. Housing prices and commuting expenses in major cities place severe financial strain on young households. With initial moving grants and remote-work opportunities, newcomers can secure spacious housing at lower monthly costs while contributing skills to regional businesses.
In conclusion, well-designed relocation subsidies benefit both revitalizing rural regions and overburdened urban households.
items.translation:
私は大都市の住民が地方地域へ移住することを促すため、政府は財政的優遇措置を提供すべきだと考えます。
第一に、そのような支援は地域の公共サービスの維持に役立ちます。多くの地方の町は急速な人口減少に直面し、学校や診療所、バス路線の閉鎖を余儀なくされています。現役世代の世帯を呼び込めば地方税収と需要が増え、自治体が全住民に不可欠なサービスを維持しやすくなります。
第二に、移住支援は過密な大都市圏における高い生活費の負担を和らげます。大都市の住宅価格や通勤費は若い世帯に重い経済的負担を与えています。初期の移住補助金とリモートワークの機会があれば、移住者は毎月の費用を抑えて広い住居を確保しつつ、地域企業に技能で貢献できます。
結論として、適切に設計された移住補助金は、再生を目指す地方と負担の大きい都市世帯の双方に利益をもたらします。
items.explanation: POINTSから「Local public services」と「Cost of living」の2点を選択し、序論（賛成の立場）→本論1（人口減少下の学校・医療・交通維持）→本論2（都市部の住居・通勤コスト緩和とリモートワーク活用）→結論の4段落構成・132語で論理的に展開しています。
rubric: POINTSから2つの観点を明確に選び4段落構成（序論・本論2つ・結論）で論じた
各本論段落で主張→背景・具体説明→帰結の論理展開を行った
準1級にふさわしい語彙・構文を正確に用いた
120〜150語の目安に収まっている

items.prompt: The inquiry concluded that the bridge failure resulted not from a single storm, but from years of (     ) maintenance.

affluentは「裕福な」。

items.translation: 調査は、橋の崩落は一度の暴風雨ではなく長年のずさんな保守管理に起因すると結論づけました。

items.prompt: To prevent conflicts of interest, board members must (     ) any financial ties they have to bidding contractors.

items.translation: 利益相反を防ぐため、理事は入札業者とのいかなる金銭的関係も開示しなければなりません。

items.prompt: Although the diplomat's remarks sounded cordial, they contained an (     ) warning against further border restrictions.

distractorReasons: implicitは「暗黙の、言外に含まれた」でcordialとの対比に合う。

items.prompt: Several coastal municipalities have formed a coalition to (     ) the central government for stronger seawall funding.

items.prompt: Hospital administrators introduced staggered shifts to (     ) the bottleneck at the pharmacy counter around noon.

items.translation: 食用キノコと有毒な近縁種が驚くほど似ているため、熟練の植物学者でさえ見誤ることがあります。

passage.title: Why Automated Translations Still Struggle with Municipal Notices
passage.text:
Local governments increasingly use automated translation tools to publish storm alerts, waste-sorting rules, and clinic schedules in dozens of languages within seconds. Compared with waiting days for external agencies to translate routine updates, instant software appears both economical and inclusive. Yet emergency managers have learned that linguistic fluency on screen can mask dangerous misunderstandings.

Public notices are full of compressed local shorthand. A message stating that "riverside shelters open following level-three advisories" assumes readers already know the municipal warning scale, while a phrase like "collection suspended pending road clearance" can be rendered grammatically yet ambiguously in another language. Machine systems trained predominantly on general web text often smooth over uncertain terms into confident-sounding sentences. Readers may therefore fail to realize that a crucial condition has been (19).

Several cities have responded not by abandoning translation software, but by changing how source notices are written in the first place. Officials draft announcements using controlled templates that avoid idioms, spell out dates and locations explicitly, and separate instructions from background explanations. Bilingual community reviewers then audit high-stakes safety templates in advance. (20), routine updates such as revised opening hours can be inserted into verified structures with far fewer errors.

The broader lesson is that translation quality begins upstream of the algorithm. Treating automated output as a finished public service risks confusing speed with comprehension, whereas pairing structured source writing with human oversight allows agencies to (21).

passage.title: Why Automated Translations Still Struggle with Municipal Notices
passage.text:
Local governments increasingly use automated translation tools to publish storm alerts, waste-sorting rules, and clinic schedules in dozens of languages within seconds. Public notices are full of compressed local shorthand. The broader lesson is that translation quality begins upstream of the algorithm. Treating automated output as a finished public service risks confusing speed with comprehension, whereas pairing structured source writing with human oversight allows agencies to (21).

passage.title: The Hidden Bias in Citizen Pothole Apps
passage.text:
Many municipal governments now offer smartphone applications that let residents photograph damaged pavement, broken streetlights, or blocked drains and send the exact GPS coordinates to repair crews. At first glance, crowdsourced reporting looks like a triumph of responsive governance: problems are spotted faster than inspectors could patrol every street, and citizens can track repair progress online.

When urban researchers compared app submissions against independent street-condition surveys across an entire city, however, a troubling discrepancy emerged. Wealthier districts with younger, tech-savvy commuters generated four times as many reports per kilometer of damaged road as older, lower-income neighborhoods where fewer residents used municipal apps or trusted rapid official action. Dispatching crews strictly in the order reports arrived meant that technology had inadvertently (22).

Recognizing this pattern did not mean shutting down the reporting platform. Citizen photos still saved inspectors valuable time on urgent hazards such as fallen branches after a storm. Instead, the public works department combined app reports with scheduled baseline inspections weighted toward neighborhoods with older infrastructure and historically low reporting rates. (23), maintenance budgets were no longer driven solely by who complained fastest on a smartphone.

Digital participation tools often promise neutrality because anyone is theoretically free to download them. Yet equal permission to use a channel rarely produces equal representation in the resulting dataset. Responsible public administration therefore requires officials to (24) before turning user-generated maps into spending priorities.

passage.title: Why Negative Scientific Results Deserve Publication
passage.text:
Pick up almost any prominent scientific journal and you will read predominantly about experiments that worked: a compound that slowed disease progression in mice, a teaching intervention that raised test scores, or a catalyst that accelerated a chemical reaction. Studies in which a plausible hypothesis produced no statistically meaningful effect are far more likely to remain unpublished in laboratory drawers—a phenomenon methodologists call the "file-drawer problem."

This publication pattern rarely stems from deliberate dishonesty. Journals compete for attention and citations, editors favor striking breakthroughs, and researchers under career pressure understandably prioritize manuscripts with a high chance of acceptance. Writing up a rigorous null result takes nearly as much time as writing up a positive discovery, yet brings far less professional recognition. Individual incentives therefore align to filter out negative findings.

The collective cost to science, however, is substantial. When five independent laboratories test the same promising idea and four find no effect while one obtains a positive result by chance, publishing only the fifth study creates a distorted impression of effectiveness. Other teams may then spend years and public grant money repeating dead-end experiments they had no way of knowing had already failed. Worse still, clinical or policy reviews that pool published studies risk overestimating the benefits of an intervention.

One promising reform is the "registered report." Under this format, peer reviewers evaluate a study's research question, sample size, and experimental protocol before data are collected. If the design is sound and the question important, the journal commits in principle to publishing the paper regardless of how the numbers turn out, provided the researchers follow the approved plan. Early evaluations suggest that registered reports contain a much higher proportion of null findings than conventional journals while maintaining high methodological quality.

Registered reports do not suit purely exploratory research where methods evolve mid-experiment, nor do they eliminate the need for replication. Yet they address a structural flaw that exhortations to individual virtue cannot fix alone: shifting prestige from whether a result looks dramatic to whether an investigation was worth conducting and carefully executed.
passage.translation: 有力な科学誌を手に取れば、病気の進行を抑えた化合物や成績を上げた教育法など「うまくいった実験」ばかりが目に入る。もっともらしい仮説を検証したが統計的に有意な効果が出なかった研究は研究室の引き出しに眠りやすく、方法論研究者はこれを「ファイル・ドロワー（お蔵入り）問題」と呼ぶ。この偏りは必ずしも悪意から生じるわけではない。雑誌は注目や引用数を競い、編集者は劇的な発見を好み、業績評価にさらされる研究者も採択率の高い原稿を優先する。厳密な「効果なし（帰無結果）」の論文を書く労力は陽性結果とほぼ同じなのに評価が低いため、個人の合理的行動が陰性結果をふるい落としてしまうのだ。しかし科学全体への代償は大きい。5つの独立した研究室が同じ仮説を試し4つが効果なし、1つが偶然陽性になったとき、5番目だけが公刊されれば有効性が歪んで伝わる。他のチームはすでに失敗したと知る由もなく同じ行き止まりの実験に公的資金と年月を費やし、公刊論文を統合する医療・政策レビューも効果を過大評価しかねない。有望な改革の一つが「事前登録査読（レジスタード・レポート）」だ。データ収集前に研究の問いと標本数、手順を査読し、設計が妥当で問いが重要なら結果がどう出ようと原則掲載を約束する仕組みである。探索的研究には向かない面もあるが、結果の派手さではなく「問う価値があり厳密に遂行されたか」へ評価軸を移す構造的な改善策となっている。

passage.title: Why Negative Scientific Results Deserve Publication
passage.text:
Pick up almost any prominent scientific journal and you will read predominantly about experiments that worked: a compound that slowed disease progression in mice, a teaching intervention that raised test scores, or a catalyst that accelerated a chemical reaction. Studies in which a plausible hypothesis produced no statistically meaningful effect are far more likely to remain unpublished in laboratory drawers—a phenomenon methodologists call the "file-drawer problem."

This publication pattern rarely stems from deliberate dishonesty. Journals compete for attention and citations, editors favor striking breakthroughs, and researchers under career pressure understandably prioritize manuscripts with a high chance of acceptance. Writing up a rigorous null result takes nearly as much time as writing up a positive discovery, yet brings far less professional recognition. Individual incentives therefore align to filter out negative findings.

The collective cost to science, however, is substantial. When five independent laboratories test the same promising idea and four find no effect while one obtains a positive result by chance, publishing only the fifth study creates a distorted impression of effectiveness. Other teams may then spend years and public grant money repeating dead-end experiments they had no way of knowing had already failed. Worse still, clinical or policy reviews that pool published studies risk overestimating the benefits of an intervention.

One promising reform is the "registered report." Under this format, peer reviewers evaluate a study's research question, sample size, and experimental protocol before data are collected. If the design is sound and the question important, the journal commits in principle to publishing the paper regardless of how the numbers turn out, provided the researchers follow the approved plan. Early evaluations suggest that registered reports contain a much higher proportion of null findings than conventional journals while maintaining high methodological quality.

Registered reports do not suit purely exploratory research where methods evolve mid-experiment, nor do they eliminate the need for replication. Yet they address a structural flaw that exhortations to individual virtue cannot fix alone: shifting prestige from whether a result looks dramatic to whether an investigation was worth conducting and carefully executed.

items.prompt: How does the "registered report" format change the publication process?
choices: It commits to publishing a study based on its prior design and question quality before outcomes are known.
It accepts only purely exploratory studies whose methods change every week.
It requires authors to guarantee a dramatic breakthrough before collecting data.
It removes peer review completely to speed up publication.
items.explanation: データ収集前に問いの重要性と実験設計を査読し、計画通りに実施されれば結果の成否にかかわらず原則掲載を約束する。
distractorReasons: 第4段落の仕組みと完全に一致する。
探索的研究（exploratory research）には向かないと最終段落で述べている。
劇的な結果の保証を求めるのとは正反対。
事前査読を行うのであり査読廃止ではない。
items.translation: 「事前登録査読（レジスタード・レポート）」形式は出版プロセスをどのように変えますか。

items.prompt: What unintended consequence did twentieth-century stream straightening produce?
choices: Water remained trapped on hillside farms for months.
Accelerated tributary flows converged downstream in sharper flood peaks and eroded habitats.
Native trout populations multiplied excessively in deep uniform channels.
Groundwater levels rose so high that summer droughts disappeared.
items.explanation: 直線化がパイプのように雨水を加速させ、複数支流の水が下流の町へ同時に集中して激しい洪水ピークを生み、川底の産卵場浸食や地下水位低下も招いた。

第2段落の洪水ピーク集中と川床浸食・生態系破壊の記述と完全に一致する。
マスの産卵場は破壊された。
地下水位は低下し夏に乾きやすくなった。
items.translation: 20世紀の河川直線化はどのような意図せざる結果を招きましたか。

passage.title: Repairing Rivers by Slowing Them Down
passage.text:
For much of the twentieth century, river engineering in agricultural valleys followed a straightforward logic: get rainwater off fields and out to sea as rapidly as possible. Winding streams were straightened into deep uniform channels, riverside marshes were drained, and fallen trees were cleared away so nothing obstructed flow. Locally, these measures turned wet meadows into productive farmland and reduced minor seasonal inundation along adjacent fields.

Downstream towns, however, paid an unexpected price. Straightened channels acted like smooth pipes, accelerating runoff from hillside storms so water from multiple tributaries arrived at urban bridges simultaneously in sharp, destructive peaks. At the same time, fast-moving currents scoured gravel from streambeds, destroying spawning habitats for native trout and lowering surrounding groundwater tables so pastures dried out faster during summer droughts.

Over the past two decades, hydrologists have tested an approach that reverses parts of this legacy without rebuilding vast concrete dams. Working in upper catchments where streams are still small, teams install "leaky woody structures"—bundles of felled logs pinned securely across channels with gaps underneath. During normal weather, base flow passes freely beneath the logs so fish can migrate unhindered. When heavy rain swells the stream, the logs intercept the upper layer of water, nudging it temporarily onto rough woodland floodplains and shallow storage ponds.

Individually, a single log barrier holds back only a modest volume. Across dozens of headwater streams, however, hundreds of small delays desynchronize tributary peaks, flattening the flood wave that eventually reaches downstream towns. Sediment and organic matter also settle behind the structures, gradually rebuilding varied streambeds where aquatic insects thrive.

Implementing natural flood management nonetheless involves delicate negotiation. Upstream landowners bear the inconvenience of saturated corners of pasture or woodland, whereas the greatest financial protection accrues to homeowners miles downstream. Expecting farmers to host water out of goodwill alone rarely succeeds at scale. Successful catchment partnerships therefore pair hydrological modeling with multi-year stewardship payments, clear liability rules if timber shifts, and joint monitoring that lets farmers see measurable effects on summer soil moisture as well as downstream flood peaks.
passage.translation: 20世紀の大半において農業地帯の河川工学は「雨水を農地から海へ一刻も早く流す」という明快な論理に従っていた。蛇行する小川は深く均一な直線水路に改修され、湿地は干拓され、流木は撤去された。局所的には湿った草地が生産性の高い農地になり周辺の軽微な冠水も減ったが、下流の町は思わぬ代償を払った。直線水路が滑らかな管のように雨水を加速させ、複数の支流からの水が都市の橋へ同時に押し寄せて破壊的な洪水のピークを生んだのだ。さらに急流が川底の砂利を削り取り、在来マスの産卵場を奪い、地下水位まで下げて夏の干ばつ時に牧草地を乾きやすくした。過去20年間、水文学者は巨大ダムを新設せずにこの負の遺産を改める手法を試してきた。上流の小さな支流に、下部に隙間を空けて丸太の束を固定する「透過型木製構造物（リーキー・ダム）」を多数設置するのだ。平時は丸太の下を水が自由に流れ魚の移動も妨げないが、大雨で増水すると上層の水を受け止めて一時的に森林の氾濫原や浅い遊水池へ逃がす。1基あたりの貯水量はわずかでも、数十の源流に何百もの小さな遅れを作ることで支流ごとのピーク時刻をずらし、下流の町に届く洪水波をなだらかにできる。もっとも上流の地主が一時的な冠水の不便を負う一方、最大の経済的恩恵は何マイルも下流の住宅所有者が受けるため、善意だけに頼っては広がらない。成功している流域連携では、複数年の管理補償金、流木移動時の明確な責任規定、そして夏の土壌水分保持効果も農家が実感できる共同モニタリングを組み合わせている。

items.prompt: How do "leaky woody structures" function differently in normal weather versus heavy rain?
choices: They block fish migration in dry weather but float away during storms.
They let ordinary flow and fish pass underneath while diverting high water onto floodplains.
They pump groundwater into concrete pipes only during winter.
They seal the streambed completely so no sediment can ever settle.
items.explanation: 平常時は丸太の下の隙間を水と魚が通り抜け、大雨による増水時のみ上層の水をせき止めて一時的に周辺の森林氾濫原や遊水池へ広げる。
distractorReasons: 平時は魚の移動を妨げず、かつ丸太はしっかり固定（pinned securely）されている。
第3段落の機能説明と正確に一致する。
コンクリート管へ地下水をくみ上げる装置ではない。
土砂や有機物は構造物の背後に堆積し多様な川床を再生する。
items.translation: 「透過型木製構造物」は平常時と大雨時でどのように働きが異なりますか。

items.prompt: Why are hundreds of small barriers across headwater streams effective?
choices: Each single log barrier can hold as much water as a giant concrete dam.
Together they stagger the timing of tributary flows, lowering the peak reaching towns.

They permanently dry up downstream rivers throughout the year.

9割を蒸発させるわけではない。
下流の川を年中干上がらせるわけではない。
items.translation: 源流域に何百もの小さな構造物を設けることが有効なのはなぜですか。

Straightened channels acted like smooth pipes, accelerating runoff from hillside storms so water from multiple tributaries arrived at urban bridges simultaneously in sharp, destructive peaks. At the same time, fast-moving currents scoured gravel from streambeds, destroying spawning habitats for native trout and lowering surrounding groundwater tables so pastures dried out faster during summer droughts.

Over the past two decades, hydrologists have tested an approach that reverses parts of this legacy without rebuilding vast concrete dams. Working in upper catchments where streams are still small, teams install "leaky woody structures"—bundles of felled logs pinned securely across channels with gaps underneath. During normal weather, base flow passes freely beneath the logs so fish can migrate unhindered. When heavy rain swells the stream, the logs intercept the upper layer of water, nudging it temporarily onto rough woodland floodplains and shallow storage ponds.

Individually, a single log barrier holds back only a modest volume. Across dozens of headwater streams, however, hundreds of small delays desynchronize tributary peaks, flattening the flood wave that eventually reaches downstream towns. Sediment and organic matter also settle behind the structures, gradually rebuilding varied streambeds where aquatic insects thrive.

Implementing natural flood management nonetheless involves delicate negotiation. Upstream landowners bear the inconvenience of saturated corners of pasture or woodland, whereas the greatest financial protection accrues to homeowners miles downstream. Expecting farmers to host water out of goodwill alone rarely succeeds at scale. Successful catchment partnerships therefore pair hydrological modeling with multi-year stewardship payments, clear liability rules if timber shifts, and joint monitoring that lets farmers see measurable effects on summer soil moisture as well as downstream flood peaks.
passage.translation: 20世紀の大半において農業地帯の河川工学は「雨水を農地から海へ一刻も早く流す」という明快な論理に従っていた。蛇行する小川は深く均一な直線水路に改修され、湿地は干拓され、流木は撤去された。局所的には湿った草地が生産性の高い農地になり周辺の軽微な冠水も減ったが、下流の町は思わぬ代償を払った。直線水路が滑らかな管のように雨水を加速させ、複数の支流からの水が都市の橋へ同時に押し寄せて破壊的な洪水のピークを生んだのだ。さらに急流が川底の砂利を削り取り、在来マスの産卵場を奪い、地下水位まで下げて夏の干ばつ時に牧草地を乾きやすくした。過去20年間、水文学者は巨大ダムを新設せずにこの負の遺産を改める手法を試してきた。上流の小さな支流に、下部に隙間を空けて丸太の束を固定する「透過型木製構造物（リーキー・ダム）」を多数設置するのだ。平時は丸太の下を水が自由に流れ魚の移動も妨げないが、大雨で増水すると上層の水を受け止めて一時的に森林の氾濫原や浅い遊水池へ逃がす。1基あたりの貯水量はわずかでも、数十の源流に何百もの小さな遅れを作ることで支流ごとのピーク時刻をずらし、下流の町に届く洪水波をなだらかにできる。もっとも上流の地主が一時的な冠水の不便を負う一方、最大の経済的恩恵は何マイルも下流の住宅所有者が受けるため、善意だけに頼っては広がらない。成功している流域連携では、複数年の管理補償金、流木移動時の明確な責任規定、そして夏の土壌水分保持効果も農家が実感できる共同モニタリングを組み合わせている。

items.prompt: 以下の英文を読んで、その内容を英語で要約し、解答欄に記入しなさい。本文にない自分の意見は加えないこと。（目安語数：60〜70語）

passage.title: Dynamic Pricing at Cultural Institutions
passage.text:
Traditionally, art museums and science centers charged flat admission fees throughout the year, setting one standard ticket price regardless of the day or hour. Recently, however, several major institutions have adopted dynamic pricing, raising ticket prices during peak weekend afternoons and school holidays while offering discounted entry on quiet weekday mornings or late afternoons.

Administrators argue that variable pricing spreads visitor numbers more evenly across the week. Overcrowded galleries become calmer and safer, while extra revenue from peak-hour tourists helps fund building conservation and educational programs. Lower off-peak rates can also attract retirees, students, and flexible local residents.

Critics, on the other hand, warn that higher weekend prices penalize working families who can visit only on Saturdays or Sundays, potentially turning public cultural spaces into luxuries during prime hours. To address this concern, some museums pair dynamic pricing with free monthly family Sundays or reserved low-cost community tickets.
passage.translation:
従来、美術館や科学館は曜日や時間帯にかかわらず年間を通じて一律の入館料を設定していた。しかし近年、複数の主要施設がダイナミック・プライシング（変動料金制）を導入し、混雑する週末午後や長期休みの料金を引き上げる一方、空いている平日午前や夕方に割引料金を提供している。
運営側は、変動料金によって来館者数が週全体に分散され、過密だった展示室が落ち着いて安全になるほか、繁忙期の観光客からの増収が施設保全や教育事業の財源になり、閑散期の低料金が学生や高齢者らを呼び込めると主張する。
一方で批判派は、週末の値上げは土日にしか来館できない共働き・子育て世帯に不利益を与え、公共の文化空間を贅沢品に変えかねないと警告する。この懸念に対処するため、月1回の家族無料日曜や地域向け低額枠を併用する館も出ている。

items.model: Instead of charging flat admission fees, several museums now use dynamic pricing, raising peak period ticket rates while discounting quiet weekday hours. Supporters note that this spreads attendance, funds conservation and education, and attracts local visitors during quiet hours. However, critics warn higher weekend fees burden working families with limited schedules, prompting some institutions to preserve public access through free family days or affordable community tickets.
items.translation: 一律の入館料の代わりに、繁忙期の料金を上げ空いている平日時間帯を割り引く変動料金制を導入する博物館が増えている。支持者は来館者の分散や保全・教育財源の確保、閑散時間帯の地域客誘致を挙げる。一方、週末の値上げは予定の限られる働く世帯の負担になるとの批判もあり、家族無料日や手頃な地域向け券で公共の機会を守る施設もある。
items.explanation: 第1段落の導入（一律料金から繁忙期値上げ・閑散期割引の変動料金制への移行）、第2段落の利点（混雑分散・財源確保・閑散期集客）、第3段落の批判と対策（週末しか来られない働く世帯への負担と無料日・手頃な地域枠の併用）を66語で的確に要約しています。
rubric: 一律料金から変動料金制への移行を冒頭で明確に示した
運営側の挙げる利点（混雑緩和・財源・閑散期誘客）を含めた
働く世帯への不利益という批判と無料日等の緩和策を含めた
主観を交えず自分の語句で60〜70語の範囲に収めた

items.prompt:
次のTOPICについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ書きなさい。POINTSから2つを選び、序論・本論（2つ）・結論の構成で論述しなさい。（目安語数：120〜150語）
TOPIC: Should universities require all undergraduate students to complete an internship before graduating?
POINTS:
• Career readiness
• Academic study time
• Financial burden
• Regional inequality
items.model:
I do not believe universities should require every undergraduate student to complete an internship before graduating.
First, making internships compulsory can reduce essential academic study time. Many university majors, such as laboratory sciences, history, and mathematics, demand intensive reading, experiments, and thesis writing. Forcing all students to spend weeks off campus may interrupt deep theoretical learning that only universities can provide.
Second, a mandatory requirement creates an unfair financial burden and regional inequality. Meaningful internships are often concentrated in major cities and are sometimes unpaid or low-paid. Students who support themselves through part-time jobs or study in rural areas would face heavy travel and living expenses.
In conclusion, while optional internships should be supported, universities should not make them a graduation requirement for everyone.
items.translation:
私は大学がすべての学部生に卒業前のインターンシップ修了を義務づけるべきではないと考えます。
第一に、インターンシップの義務化は不可欠な学業の研究時間を削りかねません。実験科学や歴史学、数学など多くの専攻では集中的な読書や実験、卒業論文の執筆が求められます。全員に数週間の学外活動を強制すれば、大学でしか得られない深い理論的学習が中断される恐れがあります。
第二に、一律の義務化は不公平な経済的負担や地域格差を生みます。有意義なインターン先は大都市に集中しがちで、無給または低賃金の場合もあります。アルバイトで生計を立てている学生や地方で学ぶ学生は重い交通費・滞在費に直面してしまいます。
結論として、任意のインターン支援は充実させるべきですが、全員の卒業要件にすべきではありません。
items.explanation: 反対の立場を明確にとり、POINTSから「Academic study time」と「Financial burden（＋Regional inequality）」を選んで4段落構成・129語で説得力高く展開しています。
rubric: POINTSから2つの観点を明確に取り上げ4段落構成で論じた
学問上の専門性や学生間の経済・地理的条件を具体的に掘り下げた
準1級にふさわしい語彙（compulsory, intensive, mandatory等）を正確に用いた
120〜150語の目安に収まっている
